title: Introduce lazy provider initialization and split networking blueprints to reduce Terraform plan churn
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We continue to see significant Terraform plan churn and frequent provider-induced diffs across environment overlays. Root causes identified: 1) provider blocks are duplicated across many module entrypoints leading to re-initialization and drift; 2) networking blueprints mix core, region, and ephemeral resources in the same overlays which increases plan scope for routine changes; 3) older AWS provider version constraints prevent us from leveraging provider-side stability improvements (parallelism and resource hashing fixes).

Goal: Reduce noisy plans and plan times by introducing a lazy provider initialization pattern (centralized provider binding + opt-in lazy_init wrappers) and by splitting networking blueprints into a small core (VPC, core routing, shared security) and lightweight per-overlay overlays (ephemeral subnets, test NATs, route53). This ticket covers design, implementation, CI gating, and initial rollout to staging.

Scope:
- Add a provider-lookup module that centralizes provider configuration and exposes a thin provider passthrough for submodules.
- Implement lazy_init helpers to avoid immediate provider attachment for modules that only declare data sources or read-only resources during plan. This mirrors earlier experiments in a POC branch.
- Rework two networking blueprints (prod and staging) to split core and overlay layers and migrate transient resources to overlays.
- Upgrade aws provider constraint to "\>= 5.14.0, \< 6.0.0" in root and provider-lookup module and verify compatibility with downstream modules.
- Add CI plan diffs for each environment and a staging-only rollout before production.

Success criteria:
- Average terraform plan time for networking changes reduced by \>= 30% in staging.
- Number of unrelated diffs in networking PRs reduced by \>= 50% over a 4-week window.
- No state drift or resource replacement in prod after rollout.

Acceptance criteria:
- Design doc reviewed and approved by infra leads.
- PRs with unit tests (terraform validate, tflint) and CI plan checks pass.
- Migration scripts for state moves documented and smoke-tested in staging.

Rollback strategy: Revert to previous provider bindings and keep isolated overlay for a hotfix path. State moves are reversible via state snapshot and targeted terraform import steps documented.

2025-11-07 - Lina Chen (Infra Lead): Reviewed design. Requested explicit state migration steps for the two resources that will move between core and overlay (shared-nat-gw and cross-account-route).

2025-11-11 - QA: Ran staging plan checks using feature branch. Observed a plan showing replacement of a secondary NAT due to lifecycle block differences — added lifecycle ignore_changes for ephemeral tags and re-ran. Plan now clean in staging for the tested changes.
2025-11-12 - Diego Morales: Updated PRs to include state-move helper script and documented step-by-step in description. Requesting review from Lina and Security for provider constraint bump.
